generator.description: Expected reduction and fix for reference-philadelphia-2star.

frame.definition: Apparent geocentric of date (CONVENTIONS section 7): true equator and equinox of date.
excludes: diurnal aberration (this is a geocentric frame; the observer is not moving in it)
topocentric parallax (CONVENTIONS section 5 applies it as an altitude correction)
frame.gha_sign: west-positive, [0, 360), as tabulated in the Nautical Almanac
includes: precession and nutation to the true equator and equinox of date (Skyfield's IAU 2000A/2006 model)
relativistic light deflection by the Sun
stellar proper motion and annual parallax from the Hipparcos catalogue (stars)

generator.never_a_runtime_dependency: Generated by tools/reference/ (Python + Skyfield). CONVENTIONS section 11: never regenerate a fixture from Rust output.
generator.refraction: none. Every altitude here is already Ho (altitude_kind observed_ho), so the CONVENTIONS section 5 chain runs no steps.

timescale.delta_t_source: Skyfield's bundled skyfield/data/iers.npz, a daily Delta-T table built from the IERS finals2000A.all series at the time the Skyfield wheel was released. Outside the table Skyfield extrapolates with its long-term Delta-T model (Morrison & Stephenson / Espenak & Meeus).
timescale.dut1_definition: DUT1 = UT1 - UTC = 32.184 + Delta_AT - Delta_T, as Skyfield derives it
timescale.leap_second_table: bundled in the same iers.npz; latest offset 37 s from 2017-01-01
timescale.warning_dut1: CONVENTIONS section 6 assumes DUT1 = 0. Skyfield does not: every GHA in these fixtures uses Skyfield's UT1. The per-epoch dut1_s is recorded, and gha_deg_dut1_zero gives the same GHA recomputed with UT1 = UTC so a DUT1 = 0 implementation has a directly comparable number. 1 s of DUT1 = 15.0410686 arcsec of GHA. Beyond the Delta-T table's end the extrapolated Delta-T implies |DUT1| far above the 0.9 s that real leap seconds enforce (about -3.5 s at 2055), so gha_deg alone is not a physically meaningful prediction for far-future epochs; gha_deg_dut1_zero is.

generator.tolerance_justification: The per-sight tolerance is the session's own sigma, 0.1 arcmin. The position tolerance is 10 m (see position_tolerance_m) and is a numerical regression target on clean, well-conditioned synthetic geometry, exactly as docs/BRIEF.md 'Validation that matters' states. It is NOT a claim about field accuracy: no real sextant, horizon or clock is involved anywhere in this file.

name: reference-philadelphia-2star
notes: At 2026-10-01T01:30:00Z, 18 of the 58 navigational stars are above 15 deg at the truth position. The five used here were chosen for azimuth spread (largest gap 88.5 deg) with every altitude between 36.9 and 61.1 deg, clear of both the CONVENTIONS section 5 low-altitude refraction flag at 10 deg and the near-zenith azimuth singularity. Full list of candidates, sorted by azimuth: Polaris (alt 39.95, az 0.82); Schedar (alt 51.98, az 45.70); Mirfak (alt 26.97, az 46.03); Hamal (alt 26.00, az 80.08); Alpheratz (alt 51.64, az 91.81); Markab (alt 54.50, az 125.42); Fomalhaut (alt 15.97, az 155.15); Enif (alt 58.94, az 162.15); Nunki (alt 17.04, az 210.63); Altair (alt 54.62, az 213.97); Rasalhague (alt 36.07, az 254.95); Vega (alt 61.07, az 280.06); Alphecca (alt 21.66, az 287.24); Eltanin (alt 55.37, az 305.68); Alkaid (alt 18.34, az 319.68); Deneb (alt 82.75, az 320.59); Alioth (alt 17.12, az 330.58); Kochab (alt 36.94, az 339.95).

Every observation supplies `geocentric` directly, so no ephemeris provider runs and the session tests the solver alone (docs/BRIEF.md, 'First numerical slice'). The reducer must emit Warning::SuppliedDirectionUsed for each sight.

`altitude_kind` is `observed_ho`: the CONVENTIONS section 5 chain must run no steps at all. Index correction, height of eye, semidiameter and horizontal parallax are all zero, so nothing has to be ignored and no AlreadyCorrected warning is warranted -- but re-reducing must still be a no-op, never a second subtraction.

The assumed position (40.5000, -74.5000) is deliberately about 83 km from the truth, with role `initializer`. A converged fix must be independent of it. If the reported position moves toward the assumed position, the initializer has leaked in as a prior.

`gha_deg` here is Skyfield's, computed with its own UT1 (DUT1 = +0.0934 s at this instant). That does not matter for this session, because the direction is supplied rather than computed: the altitudes were generated from these same GHA values, so the session is internally consistent whatever an ephemeris provider would have said. A session that omitted `geocentric` would expose the CONVENTIONS section 6 DUT1 = 0 assumption; this one does not.
kind is `simulated` and there is zero added noise. The truth lives in fixtures/expected/<name>.truth.json and must never be read by the solver or by the CLI `solve` command.

Expected result kind: `ambiguous`. Two sights and two unknowns: dof = 0, both intersections fit exactly, and neither may be promoted. CONVENTIONS section 8 requires all candidates returned and no ellipse (dof = 0 cannot support one).

The two intersections are 6023 km apart. Both are listed in `circle_intersections`, computed analytically in Python from the two circles of position, independently of the solver. The solver's multistart must find both; finding only the one near the initializer is the failure this fixture exists to catch, and the assumed position is deliberately near the truth-side intersection to make that failure look like success.

Both sights are in the western half of the sky (azimuths 214.0 and 280.1 deg, 66.1 deg apart), which is also why the geometry is poor: a wide azimuth gap is what makes the second intersection close enough to matter.
